topic: Why a naive transpose runs at a third of copy bandwidth.
goal: Explain the cache-line cost of a strided write and why tiling fixes it.
grill: My naive transpose runs at 73 GB/s while a copy kernel gets 242 GB/s.
I want the reason, not a tiled kernel to paste.
I think the naive kernel is slow because it does too much arithmetic.

facts.claim: A copy kernel is fast because each warp reads and writes contiguous addresses.
A transpose swaps the row and column indices of every element.
A naive transpose writes a column per warp, so each write touches a separate cache line; the kernel is limited by memory sectors, not arithmetic.
facts.wrong: The naive transpose is slow because it does too many arithmetic operations.

commandOutput: naive 1.821 ms 73.7 GB/s; copy 0.554 ms 242.2 GB/s
